Challenge active chamber lifting and controlled lowering so the free leg can accelerate and recover while the other leg supplies the rotational base. Stand upright with a secure band loop at the forefeet, the support foot anchoring its end and optional light fingertip contact on a stable support. Raise the bent knee to a comfortable low chamber with the pelvis quiet, then lower without swinging. Use about 1 second lifting, 2 seconds lowering and 1 second resetting. Do not use momentum, a hop or an unsecured loop. Use instead: Reduce tension or chamber height for pelvic tipping or loss of foot security. If the loop cannot be secured, use self-resisted seated bent-knee hip flexion with the hands resisting the distal thigh instead; record the changed, less reproducible resistance. Apply this change only to the same remaining combined dose and recovery; it replaces the original execution and adds no extra task or make-up attempts. This replacement uses only the remaining combined dose/rest unless explicitly stated; log changed support, event type, load and added time.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotational Press
exercises.rest: 90 s between side bouts; 10 total reps
exercises.purpose: Supply a compound unilateral push for the full-body force work while loading the connection from a freely turning foot and hip to a controlled arm press. Its diagonal pressing path complements the selected rotational task; it does not reproduce every throw path.
exercises.description: Keep the working load at 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Supply a compound unilateral push for the full-body force work while loading the connection from a freely turning foot and hip to a controlled arm press. Its diagonal pressing path complements the selected rotational task; it does not reproduce every throw path. Secure the landmine and qualify its bar, grip and minimum load. In a modest staggered stance, hold the sleeve near the rear shoulder with the rear hand. Turn the rear foot and hips into a controlled forward-and-up press, keeping wrist stacked and ribs level. No dip-drive, jump or release. Return in 3 seconds and reset without shoulder shrug or lower-back arch. Use instead: Reduce load or range for wrist, elbow or rib-position faults. If the minimum landmine setup is unsuitable, use a one-arm rotational band press from a verified anchor instead; log the changed load and setup. Apply this change only to the same remaining combined dose and recovery; it replaces the original execution and adds no extra task or make-up attempts. This replacement uses only the remaining combined dose/rest unless explicitly stated; log changed support, event type, load and added time.

explosive_progression_note: Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue retains the cued independent press from Class 32, while One-Arm Row — supported mid-range pause into fast finish adds a supported held-mid-range start to the final arm draw. The parked hip impulse and small forward scoop retain familiar force routes; the returning low roundhouse uses a familiar task and dose, but preceding work differs from its earlier prescription. Compared with Class 34, prescribed ball releases change from 13 to 6, bilateral foot-landing events change from 6 to 0, kick actions change from 0 to 4. Review actual recovery, require the held row without shoulder roll and the kick to recoil into a balanced stance, and compare only fully documented like conditions. Use a self-initiated press for remaining E1 attempts if the cue disrupts control, a full-range supported speed row for remaining E3 attempts if the partial start is strained, and a shorter kick arc for remaining E5 attempts when needed. Log those as changed executions, not matched improvement.
